title: Why your elevator always comes the wrong way
description:
On a low floor, the first elevator to reach you is going down most of the time, even though just as many cars pass you going up. One car running up and down spends the same time at every height, so if 9 of the 10 floors of shaft are above you, the car is above you 9 times in 10 when you press the button, and a car above you can only arrive going down. A second elevator only brings it to 82%; it takes many cars to get near a coin flip (Knuth, 1969). Physicists George Gamow and Marvin Stern noticed it from offices near the bottom and the top of the same building.

Numbers checked in code: 200,000 simulated button presses with 1, 2, 3 and 10 elevators (90%, 82%, 75.5%, 55% going down), matching the formula 1/2 + 1/2 x 0.8^k. Source: Wikipedia, Elevator paradox.

social_caption: Your elevator comes the wrong way 9 times in 10. It isn't bad luck: it's where the car spends its time.
facts_checked: Shaft lobby to floor 10, you on floor 1: 9 of 10 floors above you, car above you 9 in 10; up and down passes equal (50 each in 50 round trips) (verify.py)
Simulation, 200,000 presses: 1 car 90.1% down, 2 cars 82.0%, 3 cars 75.5%, 10 cars 55.3%; closed form 1/2 + 1/2 x 0.8^k (verify.py)
CTA: friend one floor below the top: car below them 9 in 10, so it arrives going up (verify.py)

Gamow (office near the bottom) and Stern (near the top) noticed the first elevator usually went down / up; one elevator spends most of its time in the larger part of the building; Knuth 1969 'The Gamow-Stern Elevator Problem': more elevators reduce the bias toward equal (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevator_paradox)

beats.say: Your elevator comes the wrong way 9 times in 10.
It's not bad luck. As many cars pass you going up as down.
You're one floor above the lobby, with 9 floors above you. You want to go up.
The car runs up and down all day. It spends the same time at every height.
Press the button at a random moment. 9 times in 10, the car is above you.
And a car above you can only arrive going down.
Add a second elevator? Still 82% the wrong way. It takes a lot of cars to reach a coin flip.
Both directions pass you equally often. You only meet the first one. George Gamow spotted this from his office near the bottom.
Your friend works one floor below the top. Which way does their elevator come?
